data.topic: portable per-project AI decision memory: vector-backed decision tracking for legacy codebases that auto-discovers implicit architectural decisions, stores them with file-level associations in a portable embedded database, and dynamically injects relevant context at edit time
data.what: Core library for per-project decision tracking with vector search + Claude Code integration layer. Auto-discovers implicit architectural decisions in legacy codebases, stores them with file-level associations, and dynamically injects relevant context when an AI is editing files.
data.audience: Kelsi's projects first, then other developers/teams using AI coding tools on legacy codebases
data.platform: CLI library + Claude Code MCP server/plugin
in_scope: Auto-discovery pipeline (AI reads code, proposes implicit decisions)
Edit-time context injection (surface relevant decisions when modifying files)
Portability across machines (clone repo, decisions work)
out_of_scope: Replacing OpenMemory (this complements it, per-project vs global)
Non-AI consumers (this is for AI coding tools, not human dashboards)
Language-specific AST parsing (start with file/function-level, not expression-level)
data.problem: Decisions are stored globally in epics.db and openmemory.sqlite, not per-project. When cloning a repo on a new machine or onboarding a new AI session, critical context about 'why the code is this way' is lost. Legacy codebases have implicit decisions that no one documented — AI tools break them because they look like bugs.
data.why: Without this, every new AI session on a legacy codebase is a liability. The AI will 'fix' intentional workarounds, violate compliance constraints it doesn't know about, and refactor away load-bearing hacks. The cost compounds with codebase size.
data.end_goal: An AI working on any file in a project automatically sees the 2-5 most relevant decisions for that file. New projects can run a discovery scan and have a populated decision store in minutes. The store travels with the repo — no external services required for basic operation.
data.complexity_reasoning: Involves unfamiliar territory: portable embedding stores without runtime model dependency, auto-discovery of implicit decisions from code, and edit-time injection patterns. Multiple external unknowns that the codebase can't answer.
